content.text: In response to backlash regarding the expansion of the Club World Cup, Fifpro submitted a legal complaint against Fifa last year, asserting that the organization had misused its position under European competition law by increasing the strain on the fixture schedule.

Tensions have escalated, as Marchi, the president of Fifpro, emphasized that although the Club World Cup 'sparked enthusiasm among many fans and showcased some of the top figures in football within a single tournament... this competition conceals a risky disconnection from the actual circumstances experienced by most footballers globally.'

Last month, senior officials from FIFA explained to BBC Sport that player welfare has been central to their decision-making process, highlighting measures like extra substitutes and permanent concussion substitutions as evidence of their commitment to this issue.

Fifa has also defended itself, with senior sources from the governing body telling BBC Sport last month the protection of player welfare has been at the core of decision-making, pointing to initiatives such as additional substitutes and permanent concussion subs.
